Seven miss classes with catchers or nothing cheap

label: The lightest playbook option check — extract --flag tokens from command carriers and require each to be a case label of the invoked repo script — resolves clean on the corrected exemplar: every flag it passes to create.sh is a case label and the unknown-option branch now exits 1. The corpus shows executable attribution, not token extraction, is the load-bearing step: non-repo flags dominate (--porcelain 165, --ff-only 20, --no-verify 20, --json 191) and flag-like tokens also appear in evidence output (four node --trace-warnings lines in the exemplar) and prose, so file-wide or fence-wide extraction without attribution would produce false violations.

The corrected literal-naming exemplar carries a live Expected-vs-producer drift: its Expected block truncates the warning to '...literal slugs.' while create.sh:1637 emits '...literal slugs describing the concrete work.' and the same document's Evidence block shows the full phrase. A token-presence literal check passes all three; whole-expected-line anchoring with dynamic segments normalized ('$_child_slug', $$, [123]) catches it. Reported, not fixed.

Wrong-value drift splits by runtime coverage: create.sh validates --level against 1,2,3,3+,phase-parent,review,research (line 95) and --phases as a positive integer (line 198) and rejects unknown options with exit 1 (line 351), so those value classes are already caught at execution; a static name check sees none of it and the cheapest shift-left reads enumerated values out of the script's own validation, while free-form values have no catcher until the command runs.

No check anywhere compares cited content to the cited line: resolveTracked returns in_range on line-count bounds alone (cite-drift-scan.mjs:294-302) and check-source-tags-helper classify() returns null (pass) for in_range (line 282), so an anchor whose target content changed in place resolves green; the cheapest candidate catcher reuses the scanner's already-extracted sentence/claim (lines 229-260) to require a distinctive claim token at the cited line, advisory only because paraphrase is legitimate.

Miss inventory and catchers for the lightest check: (1) valid flag name with a wrong value — value grammar where the script enumerates values, runtime elsewhere; (2) token-present but wrong full expected text — whole-line anchoring (exemplar case); (3) semantically wrong expectations (branch, count, ordering, exit code) — nothing cheap, needs execution and no runner exists; (4) in-range content drift — claim-token advisory; (5) flags of non-repo executables — attribution and skip, no in-repo truth; (6) commands outside fenced blocks (command-table cells) and agent/skill steps — scope extension, and only mode names are checkable against the mode registry; (7) catalog wiring coverage differs: a local bounds test reaches only the four-prefix paths the validator already resolves, a scanner consumer reaches every tracked path.

A static check that tests token presence rather than whole expected lines cannot distinguish a scenario's Expected block from the producer's actual output when the producer's line extends the expected text.
in_range is a bounds verdict, not a content verdict; a consumer that treats it as correctness has compared nothing.

Dispatch focus for iteration 3 named Q3 while the findings registry marks Q3 resolved at iteration 2 and iteration 2's own Next Focus named Q4; treated as a stale focus projection and proceeded with Q3 empirical hardening plus Q4, no halt (unattended run).

direction: File-wide or fence-wide --flag extraction without naming the invoked executable
reason: The corpus is dominated by non-repo executable flags and flag-like tokens also appear in evidence output and prose; unattributed extraction would generate false violations. A flag check is only defined once the step's executable is resolved to a tracked repo script.

direction: Failing validation on in-range anchor content mismatch
reason: Anchor prose legitimately paraphrases, so a content-at-line comparison can only be advisory (WARN); a fail-closed content gate would reject correct citations.
